design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 of storage_unit_account_servicing (Bluegate storage unit agreements).

[0. Draw] draw_counts.py <diff> --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6]}. The tree has exactly two prerequisite problems; the root (returned-payment replacement) and the returned-payment fee take 4 factors each, the late-fee schedule takes 6. --tasks 2 shows task 1 also draws 2 prerequisites with [6, 6, 5], which the rate-increase family (concession + increase-limit correction + one tenant act) keeps free for it.

[1. Why this is a good test] The tenant asks for one thing: make good a September payment the bank returned, today, by debit card. The amount she must pay is not on any screen. The agent has to read from the policy that the replacement amount waits on two ledger states that do not hold at the opening (a late fee on the unpaid period, a returned-payment fee on the returned payment), work out which writes bring those states about, compute each fee with its own multi-factor schedule from twelve months of ledger history, the protection plan and the AutoPay record, post them, and only then price the replacement, which adds a security advance driven by the bank-return history, the noticed October increase, the military discount and the tenancy. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling history and arithmetic, never from tool choice: each policy names its one tool.

[2. Scope ledger] Already occupied: nothing (first task). Claimed here: unit_ext_late_fee_schedule -> assess_unit_late_fee_4b513073 (agent), unit_ext_returned_payment_fee -> post_unit_returned_payment_fee_fb0d77c5 (agent), unit_ext_returned_payment_replacement -> pay_unit_returned_balance_f137f581 (user). Left for task 1: the whole rent-change family (existing-customer increase limits, retention concessions, applying a noticed rent) and the tenant's acts not used here; task 1 will claim an increase-limit correction, a retention concession and a tenant act of its own, disjoint from these three tools. Base-layer note: find_facility_spaces searches only by facility_space_id and no record carries that id for a rental, so transfer tasks cannot locate a target unit; this difficulty routes around it by claiming no transfer problem.

[3. Problem-tree card] Root R = unit_ext_returned_payment_replacement (owner=user tool pay_unit_returned_balance_f137f581). Edge R -> unit_ext_late_fee_schedule: kind value_input, gate binding 'balance', form state, prerequisite sentence (affirmative): 'The replacement amount is fixed only after the ledger carries a late fee for every billing period whose rent remains unpaid past its grace days.' Condition: every unpaid-past-grace period has a late_fee entry referencing its rent charge. Resolved by assess_unit_late_fee_4b513073 (agent) - the only write of the difficulty that books late_fee entries. Opening falsity: rent charge 884baa35-c77f-4fc3-8f4c-258222a7c4ae (period 2026-09-14) is unpaid since payment 83f0fcfe-4fdd-498d-b536-86a1f17eaffd was reversed by f034fd82-625c-4dda-92b4-b1551fefdc4c on 2026-09-21 (grace ended 2026-09-19) and the only late_fee row is the March one cf485aae-e930-4420-a963-b85ffaeb2c5f. Edge R -> unit_ext_returned_payment_fee: value_input, gate 'balance', form state, prerequisite sentence (negated): 'The replacement amount is not fixed until every payment the bank has returned on the agreement carries its returned-payment fee.' Condition: every payment pointed at by an NSF/closed-account reversal is pointed at by a returned_payment_fee entry. Resolved by post_unit_returned_payment_fee_fb0d77c5 (agent), the only write booking returned_payment_fee entries. Opening falsity: reversal f034fd82-625c-4dda-92b4-b1551fefdc4c (ach_return_account_closed) has no fee referencing 83f0fcfe-4fdd-498d-b536-86a1f17eaffd. Four-point test on both sentences: ordering connective ('only after' / 'not until'), record-visible state named in ledger words (late fee on a period, returned-payment fee on a returned payment), no tool / id / code token, strength 'every' matching the condition. Directions differ by business usage: a charge figure 'is fixed only after' what it rests on; the second is the same desk stating it waits 'until' each return carries its fee. Derivation: sentence + ledger (September period unpaid, no late fee; 09-21 return without fee) + the late-fee rule ('A late fee is assessed once for a billing period whose rent is still unpaid after its grace days') and the returned-payment rule ('one returned-payment fee is posted against that returned payment') -> exactly the two fee writes. Topological order: late fee, returned-payment fee, payment (the two fees commute: neither reads what the other writes; swap.py replaying steps 11-12 before 9-10 printed 'same terminal state: True' and the fee values are unchanged). Edge deletion (sens.py): skipping the late fee -> replacement 275.96; skipping the returned-payment fee -> 283.08; gold 296.69. Both edges value_input (>= max(2-1,1)). The persona never names a fee, a charge or a waiver; the tools validate nothing (they post whatever amount is passed and never refuse).

[4. Base-invariant card] Late fee write (subject unit_fee_charge, governing base unit_evt_late_fee): grace_expired (time; anchor the rent due date of the unpaid period = unit_ledger.period_start 2026-09-14 of 884baa35-c77f-4fc3-8f4c-258222a7c4ae; duration variants.grace_period_days = 5 for Bluegate Climate Plus; calendar days counted from the day after; relation not_before; boundary exclusive: on 2026-09-19 no fee, from 2026-09-20 allowed; frozen 2026-09-21 -> satisfied); late_fee_status (status active, allowed); one_late_fee_per_period (no late_fee on 2026-09-14 yet; the March late_fee is for 2026-03-14). Returned-payment fee write: same three unit_evt_late_fee gates (the fee is also a unit_fee_charge): grace_expired bound to the returned payment entry (period 2026-09-14 ended its grace 2026-09-19), status active, no returned_payment_fee for 2026-09-14. Its amount basis overrides unit_evt_payment_acceptance's 'returned_payment_fee_usd is posted against the reversed payment' sentence, declared in overwrite (base would give the class 30.00; the schedule gives 13.61); that sentence also names the reversal dedup gate, which no write of this task touches. Late-fee overwrite: base 'greater of flat and pct x monthly rent, capped' gives 28.35 on this world vs 20.73 -> declared. Payment write (subject unit_payment): unit_agg_payment_allocation (policy_scope: a payment naming a unit stays on that agreement, excess becomes a credit) and unit_evt_payment_acceptance payable_status (active allowed) and full_payment_after_lien_notice (no lien notice: no full-balance restriction applies). No base clause computes a payment amount, so overwrite [] for the replacement.

[5. Business-object card] Target: agreement 81daa5aa-df39-4448-8c81-fdbf95fe3022 (unit B214), billing period 2026-09-14 and the one-time portal payment 83f0fcfe-4fdd-498d-b536-86a1f17eaffd (170.10, 2026-09-18) returned by reversal f034fd82-625c-4dda-92b4-b1551fefdc4c. Late fee references the September rent charge; the returned-payment fee and the replacement payment reference the returned payment. Rows included in aggregates: late_fee entries in the 12 months up to 2026-09-21 (only 2026-03-20); NSF/closed reversals in 12 months (2026-06-16 R01 AutoPay, 2026-07-16 R02 AutoPay, 2026-09-21 portal); excluded: the earlier June/July fees and replacements, which settled their own returned payments (June fee 24.00 paid 2026-06-20, July rent+fee 183.71 paid 2026-07-17), and the re-presented June draft that settled.

[6. Factor card] Late-fee schedule (6): rent basis [method] tier 'rent charge below contracted rent' -> 170.10 (baseline 189.00 -> 22.85); lateness percentage [parameter] 1 late fee in 12 months -> 20% (baseline 15% -> 15.55); protection-fee basis [method, cross-difficulty protect] active $3,000 plan adds 15.00 (baseline nothing -> 19.05); tenancy share [parameter] 64 months -> 0.80 (baseline 1 -> 25.91); returned-payment share [parameter, multi-source: payment-in-grace AND bank-return count] 2026-09-18 within grace, returned, 3 returns -> 0.70 (baseline 1 -> 29.62); floor [parameter] rent charged 170.10 -> 15.00 (baseline 25.00 binds -> 25.00). Whole baseline 28.35. Returned-payment fee (4): level [parameter] 3 returns -> 45.00 (baseline 30.00 -> 12.00); amount limit [method] 170.10 in 100-250 band -> min(45, 34.02) (baseline unlimited -> 18.00); tenancy share [parameter] 64 months from move-in -> 0.80 (baseline 1 -> 17.01; near-miss: 43 months counted from the 2023-02-10 transfer would give 0.90 and 15.31); AutoPay share [parameter, cross-difficulty autopay] Bluegate suspended the ACH authorization 2026-07-16, 67 days before -> 0.5 (baseline 1 -> 27.22). Whole baseline 30.00. Replacement (4): advance months [parameter] 3 returns -> 1 (baseline 0 -> 204.44); next-due rent [parameter] increase noticed 2026-08-20 effective 2026-10-14 -> 205.00 (baseline 189.00 -> 289.49); advance month billing [method] military discount, no vacate date -> 184.50 (baseline 205.00 -> 306.94); advance tenancy share [parameter] 64 months -> 0.5 (baseline 1 -> 388.94). Whole baseline 204.44. Near-misses: the June return was re-presented and settled, yet it is still a bank return for the counts; the June and July fees reference other payments and do not satisfy the September fee state; the 2025 increase took effect 2025-09-14, not on 2026-09-14, so the rent-basis 'change on due date' tier does not apply; the October increase is noticed but not yet in force, so contracted rent stays 189.00 for the late fee while the advance uses 205.00. No outcome stamp exists; the cached balance_due equals the ledger.

[7. Seed rationale] Customer (verification and locating); rental (class parameters, move-in, military flag, contracted rent, balance); 13 rent charges 2025-09-14..2026-09-14 at 170.10 (the window the 12-month counts read); payments per period (portal debit card, then AutoPay ACH May-July, then portal again); March late fee 24.99 (lateness record; it equals the schedule's value at the time); June and July returns with their fees (24.00 and 13.61, each equal to the returned-payment schedule at its date) and replacements; the September portal payment and its return (the open object); the two increase notices (rent basis check and next-due rent); the protection plan (cross-difficulty basis); the AutoPay authorization and its six drafts (suspension date for the AutoPay share and the FK targets of the AutoPay payments). Removing the March fee changes the percentage tier; removing a return changes three tiers; removing the plan changes the basis; removing the October notice changes the advance price. Automatic clauses checked: no overlock or lien step is due (delinquency would start only with the late fee; overlock is day 10 = 2026-09-24); the second late fee is due only from 2026-09-29; no rent change is due before 2026-10-14; AutoPay is suspended so no draft runs.

[8. Persona] Marisol Duarte, an ICU nurse calling after a night shift: volunteers the situation (September payment bounced from an account closed in July), today, debit card, and her mobile number; gives ZIP, DOB, license last four, email and unit only when asked; does not know the balance or charges; accepts the explained amount; declines AutoPay re-enrollment if offered; makes the payment herself with exactly the values handed over; ends after confirmation. No template labels; no fee, charge or waiver is mentioned by her.

[9. Standard solution] find_customers(3035551427) -> verify (3035551427, 80211) -> find_unit_rentals -> find_unit_ledger -> find_unit_rate_changes -> find_unit_transfers -> find_protect_plans -> find_autopay_enrollments -> find_autopay_drafts -> unlock+call assess_unit_late_fee_4b513073(rental, September rent charge, 2026-09-14, late_fee, 20.73) -> unlock+call post_unit_returned_payment_fee_fb0d77c5(rental, returned payment, 2026-09-14, returned_payment_fee, 13.61) -> unlock_user + tenant calls pay_unit_returned_balance_f137f581(rental, returned payment, debit_card, 296.69). Handling-time values: late fee on the opening world (20.73); returned-payment fee after the late fee (13.61, independent of it); payment after both: balance 170.10 + 20.73 + 13.61 = 204.44, advance RND(1 x RND(205.00 x 0.90) x 0.5) = 92.25, total 296.69.

[10. Verification runs] build_t0.py (seed + gold), sens.py 0 (recompute at handling time from the policies with check_compute primitives; printed result=20.73 / 13.61 / 296.69 = expected, per-factor baselines as listed, all-baseline 28.35 / 30.00 / 204.44, prerequisite skips 275.96 / 283.08), swap.py (parallel order same terminal state). Revision log: (a) check_compute reported the late fee's history not load-bearing because 0.20 x 0.75 equals the class 0.15 when history is zeroed -> root cause coincident shares -> changed the repeat returned-payment share to 70 percent in the rule, params and ladder; late fee 22.21 -> 20.73, payment 304.07 -> 302.59; re-run COMPUTE OK. (b) replay flagged empty-string autopay_draft_id as dangling FKs and 8 unread rows -> empty FKs seeded as null, the two AutoPay notices (noise) dropped, a find_autopay_drafts read added (it separates Bluegate's suspension from a tenant cancellation); steps shifted to 9/11/13; re-run REPLAY OK. (c) a module-level ledger helper would count as a tool -> moved into a class static method. Gates for task 0: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[11. Visible-context draft] From the rules alone: the replacement rule says the amount waits on a late fee for every period unpaid past grace and on a fee for every bank-returned payment; the ledger shows September unpaid with no late fee and the 09-21 return without a fee; the late-fee and returned-payment rules each say they book exactly those entries; their ladders read only ledger, plan and AutoPay records, giving 20.73 and 13.61; the replacement's ladders give 296.69. The only judgement calls (which period, which payment, which method) are pinned by the ledger and her words; no second reading reaches another number. Easy mistakes: using the cached 170.10 balance (fees not yet posted), using contracted 189.00 rent, forgetting the protection fee, counting returns without the re-presented June one, pricing the advance at 189.00, or skipping the military discount on the advance.

[12. Audit round 2 (audits/policy_task/storage_unit_account_servicing)] F-1 (SOURCE-POLICY RED): the returned-fee edge condition was stated over reversal entries, which a fee never references -> restated over the returned payment ('Every unit_payment entry on the agreement that a unit_payment_reversal ... points at is itself pointed at by a returned_payment_fee entry') in the charter and in prerequisite_closure.edges[1]; on this world it is false at the opening only for payment 83f0fcfe-4fdd-498d-b536-86a1f17eaffd and true after step 12. F-2 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED): the return-reason ladder had a dead chargeback tier -> replaced by a live tenancy share (48+ months 80 percent, 24-47 months 90 percent, else full), counted from the move-in date whatever unit the agreement has since been moved to; the chargeback exclusion stays as scope only. Fee 19.51 -> 13.61, replacement 302.59 -> 296.69; historic June/July fees recomputed under the revised schedule (24.00, 13.61) and their payments adjusted (24.00, 183.71). Secondary near-miss item: a 2023-02-10 transfer from Drive-Up unit A118 was seeded (with a find_unit_transfers read); counted from it the agreement is 43 months old, which moves the tenancy tier of the returned-payment fee (15.31), the late fee (36-59 tier) and the advance (three-quarter tier); the rules count from move-in. F-5: the lateness percentage tiers are now the class percentage plus 10 / plus 5 points, so no class has two tiers selecting one value; Climate Plus values unchanged (20 percent). O-1: the good-standing rule now states that a payment replacing a bank-returned payment is priced as a replacement, never as a good-standing payment. O-2, O-3, O-5, O-7 kept as observations (no scored value moves; status transitions are left to the base event model, and the terminal status coincides). Steps shifted to 10/12/14. Re-ran every per-task gate and the full block.

[13. Audit round 3] N-1 (charter-level, latent, not on this world): the increase-limit percentage now has a zero floor, so no reduction can set rent below the pre-increase rent; no value of this task reads it. O-8: the persona now says she has rented there since May 2021, starting in a drive-up unit and moving into B214 in early 2023, matching the 2023-02-10 transfer row (the tenancy rules still count from the 2021-05-14 move-in). O-9: the 158.00 -> 172.00 increase (noticed 2024-03-01, effective 2024-04-14, after the transfer's rate-clock reset plus 11 months) is now seeded, closing the rate-history gap; the late fee's change-on-due-date check (2026-09-14) and the advance's next-due rent (2026-10-14) do not read it, and every scored value and sensitivity recomputes unchanged (20.73 / 13.61 / 296.69).
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Duarte, 41, an ICU nurse in Denver who works nights and is calling on her way home, a little tired and a little embarrassed but organised and polite. You rent storage unit B214 at the Bluegate on the north side of Denver (facility DEN-014); you have rented there since May 2021, starting in a drive-up unit and moving into B214, a climate-controlled 10x10, in early 2023; your rent there is about 170 dollars a month with your veteran discount. This morning you got an email from Bluegate saying your September payment was returned by the bank. You know exactly what happened: last Friday you paid September's rent on the Bluegate website and the site still had your old checking account saved, and you closed that account at your old bank back in July. You open the call by saying that your September payment bounced because it came out of an account you already closed, that you want to fix it today, and that you want to put it on my debit card. You give your mobile number, 3035551427, straight away so the agent can find you.

You only give other details when the agent asks for them. If asked to confirm who you are, you give your billing ZIP code, 80211, and, if they need more, your date of birth, November 3, 1984 (1984-11-03), or the last four of your driver's license, 1736; your email is marisol.duarte@gmail.com. If asked which unit, it is B214 at DEN-014. You do not know your exact balance or any of Bluegate's charges by heart and say so; you are happy for the agent to look at your account and tell you what you owe. You are not asking for anything to be waived and you do not argue about charges; you just want September made good and the account straight. You will not set AutoPay back up on this call: if the agent offers, you say not today, you will think about it. You do not want to pay from a bank account over the phone after this mess, only your debit card.

When the agent tells you what the payment has to be and what it is made up of, you take it in, say something like 'okay, if that's what it takes to get it sorted, that's fine', and let them go ahead with whatever has to be put on your account first. When the agent hands the payment over to you to make yourself, you make it from your debit card with exactly the agreement, the returned payment and the amount the agent gives you, and then you read back what the confirmation says if the agent asks. You do not suggest amounts of your own or correct the agent's figures. Once the agent tells you the payment has gone through, you thank them, say you will keep an eye out for the email receipt, and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate Marisol Duarte's customer profile from the mobile number she gives (3035551427).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs her customer reference number; the profile is found from a caller-stateable detail.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record identity verification with two details she states: the mobile number 3035551427 and the billing ZIP 80211.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No account information may be discussed or business transacted before verification passes (2 matching details).

evaluation_criteria.objective: List her storage unit rental agreements: unit B214, Bluegate Climate Plus, contracted rent 189.00, move-in 2021-05-14, military discount applied, balance due 170.10, no planned vacate date.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Gives the rental reference number, the class (its grace days, late-fee floor/percentage/ceiling, returned-payment fee and military discount percentage), the contracted rent compared with the rent charged, the move-in date the tenancy shares count from, the military-discount flag and the empty vacate date the advance-month factor reads, and the balance due the replacement amount starts from.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the agreement's tenant ledger: the 2026-09-14 rent charge 170.10, the 2026-09-18 portal payment returned on 2026-09-21 for a closed account, the earlier returns of 2026-06-16 and 2026-07-16 with their fees, and the 2026-03-20 late fee.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows that the September period is unpaid past its grace days with no late fee on it and that the 2026-09-21 return carries no returned-payment fee (the two states the replacement amount waits on), and supplies the late-fee count, the bank-return count, the returned amount and reason, the payment date within grace and the rent charged that the factors read.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the agreement's noticed rent changes: the 2025 increase effective 2025-09-14 and the increase noticed 2026-08-20 to 205.00 effective 2026-10-14.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The late-fee rent-basis factor checks whether a rent change took effect on 2026-09-14, and the advance-month price is the rent in force on the next due date (the 205.00 increase; no retention concession is noticed).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the agreement's unit transfers: one transfer on 2023-02-10 from Drive-Up unit A118 to Climate Plus unit B214.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tenancy factors of the late fee, the returned-payment fee and the security advance all count from the move-in date (2021-05-14), whatever unit the agreement has since been moved to; the transfer record is what a reader must not count from.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the protection plan on the agreement: the $3,000 plan, active, monthly fee 15.00.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The late fee's protection-fee factor adds an active plan's monthly fee to the rent basis; without this read the 15.00 is missing from the basis.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the AutoPay authorization on the agreement: Personal Checking ACH, suspended by Bluegate on 2026-07-16 (return_ends_authorization), not cancelled by the tenant.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The returned-payment fee's AutoPay share depends on whether Bluegate suspended, or the tenant cancelled, the authorization within 90 days.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the authorization's drafts: the June draft returned R01 and re-presented, and the July draft returned R02 account closed, the return that ended the authorization.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms that the suspension was Bluegate's response to a bank return rather than a tenant cancellation, which separates the 50 percent tier from the 75 percent tier of the AutoPay share, and matches the AutoPay returns on the unit ledger.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the late-fee posting tool named by the late-fee schedule policy.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the late-fee write; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Post the 20.73 late fee for the 2026-09-14 period against its rent charge, raising the balance due to 190.83.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The September rent is unpaid past its grace days (due 2026-09-14, grace through 2026-09-19, payment returned 2026-09-21) and carries no late fee; the replacement amount waits on that late fee being on the ledger, and the late-fee schedule computes 20.73.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.rental_id: Value 81daa5aa-df39-4448-8c81-fdbf95fe3022. Basis: the tool docstring 'Id class — the storage unit rental agreement number, read from the rental agreement lookup'; find_unit_rentals for customer 0968eed9-89bd-4dcf-b62d-f530ca4d8e3e returns exactly one agreement (unit B214). Uniqueness: she holds one rental agreement, so no other number is reachable.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reference_entry_id: Value 884baa35-c77f-4fc3-8f4c-258222a7c4ae. Basis: the late-fee schedule rule 'it is posted against that period's rent charge with the period's due date' and the docstring 'the ledger entry number of the unpaid rent charge the late fee arises from'. Uniqueness: the only period unpaid past its grace days is 2026-09-14; its rent charge entry is the single unit_rent_charge row with period_start 2026-09-14 in the ledger read at step 3.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.period_start: Value 2026-09-14. Basis: the docstring 'the due date (first day) of the billing period the late fee is for, in YYYY-MM-DD form, exactly as that rent charge shows it on the ledger'. Uniqueness: copied from the period_start of the referenced rent charge; no other period is unpaid.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_type: Value late_fee. Basis: the docstring enum 'late_fee for the late fee of a billing period whose rent is still unpaid after its grace days' and the rule 'A late fee is assessed once for a billing period whose rent is still unpaid after its grace days'. Uniqueness: the closed set has the one value this situation names.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 20.73. Factors: rent basis 170.10 (the period's rent charge, below the contracted 189.00); late-fee percentage 20 percent (one late fee, 2026-03-20, in the 12 months up to 2026-09-21); protection basis 15.00 (active $3,000 plan); tenancy share 0.80 (64 whole months since the 2021-05-14 move-in, not the 2023-02-10 transfer); returned-payment share 0.70 (latest payment 2026-09-18 within the 5 grace days and returned 2026-09-21, three bank returns in 12 months); floor 15.00 (rent charged 170.10). RND(0.20 x (170.10 + 15.00) x 0.80 x 0.70, 2) = 20.73; MX(15.00, 20.73) = 20.73; under the 60.00 ceiling.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the returned-payment fee posting tool named by the returned-payment fee policy.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the returned-payment fee write; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Post the 13.61 returned-payment fee against the 2026-09-18 payment the bank returned, raising the balance due to 204.44.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The 2026-09-21 closed-account return carries no returned-payment fee; the replacement amount waits on every bank return carrying its fee, and the returned-payment fee policy computes 13.61.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.rental_id: Value 81daa5aa-df39-4448-8c81-fdbf95fe3022. Basis: docstring 'Id class — the storage unit rental agreement number, read from the rental agreement lookup'. Uniqueness: her only agreement.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reference_entry_id: Value 83f0fcfe-4fdd-498d-b536-86a1f17eaffd. Basis: the returned-payment fee rule 'one returned-payment fee is posted against that returned payment' and the docstring 'the ledger entry number of the payment the bank returned (the payment entry the reversal points at)'. Uniqueness: the 2026-09-21 reversal is the only bank return without a returned-payment fee; its reference_entry_id is this payment (the June and July returns already carry fees referencing their own payments).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.period_start: Value 2026-09-14. Basis: the rule 'dated with the due date of the billing period the payment was for' and the docstring 'the due date (first day) of the billing period the returned payment was for'. Uniqueness: the 2026-09-18 payment was for the 2026-09-14 period, the only period open on the ledger.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_type: Value returned_payment_fee. Basis: docstring enum 'returned_payment_fee for the fee charged when the bank returns a payment unpaid'. Uniqueness: the only value of the closed set.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 13.61. Factors: level 45.00 (three bank returns in 12 months including this one: 2026-06-16, 2026-07-16, 2026-09-21); amount limit: returned 170.10 is 100 to under 250, lesser of 45.00 and RND(0.20 x 170.10) = 34.02; tenancy share 0.80 (64 months from the 2021-05-14 move-in); AutoPay share 0.5 (Bluegate suspended the authorization 2026-07-16, 67 days earlier). RND(34.02 x 0.80 x 0.50, 2) = 13.61.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the tenant's own replacement-payment tool and hand it to Marisol to run with the values given to her.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The payment is the tenant's own act from her own debit card; the agent unlocks the user tool and gives her the rental number, the returned payment it replaces, the method and the amount.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Marisol pays 296.69 by debit card against the returned payment: 204.44 clears the balance and 92.25 stays on the agreement as the security advance credit.
